Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 9

Rank Nation Gold Silver Bronze Total 1 China 132 53 45 230 2 Japan 41 68 63 172 3 South Korea 21 26 43 90 4 Uzbekistan 12 17 13 42 5 Kazakhstan 9 13 23 45 6 Thailand 9 8 13 30 7 Bahrain 9 2 3 14 8 Iran 8 15 9 32 9 North Korea 7 5 5 17 10 Malaysia 6 3 9 18 11 Hong Kong 5 12 17 34 12 INDIA 4 20 21 45

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: Mohit Sharma set to join CSK as bowling coach
Article Text:
File photo of Mohit Sharma. (Image: X/CSK)

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India bowler Mohit Sharma is set to join the Zaheer Khan-led Chennai Super Kings (CSK) support staff as the bowling coach starting next season.The development was confirmed by CSK CEO Kasi Viswanathan. "Mohit will join CSK as our new bowling coach. His name was recommended by our head coach Zaheer Khan. Mohit was tremendous with us as a player as well and we hope he will do a great job as bowling coach," Viswanathan told TimesofIndia.com."The next set of coaching staffs will also be recruited on Zaheer's recommendation in the coming weeks," he added.Mohit last played in the Indian Premier League ( IPL ) for the Delhi Capitals but has had two stints with CSK previously, spanning four seasons. He replaces Eric Simmons as the bowling coach.The 38-year-old Mohit has played 120 fixtures in the IPL and has 134 wickets to his name. He had a second wind of sorts during his time at Gujarat Titans, where he emerged as the side's consistent wicket-taker due to his variety and accuracy. Sharma picked up 41 wickets in the two seasons he spent at GT. He also represented Punjab Kings from 2016 to 2018.The Haryana bowler announced his retirement from professional cricket in December last year."Today, with a full heart, I announce my retirement from all formats of cricket. From representing Haryana to wearing the India jersey and playing in the IPL, this journey has been nothing short of a blessing.""A very special thank you to the Haryana Cricket Association for being the backbone of my career. And my deepest gratitude to Anirudh Sir, whose constant guidance and belief in me shaped my path in ways words cannot express.Thank you to the BCCI, my coaches, my teammates, IPL franchises, support staff and all my friends for their love and support," Mohit wrote in an emotional retirement post.His journey with the Indian team will be remembered for the 2015 World Cup under MS Dhoni, where he was the joint third-highest wicket-taker. As far as the IPL is concerned, 2014 was his best outing — he won the Purple Cap after taking 23 wickets — and it came in CSK's colours.Mohit has played 26 ODIs and eight T20Is for India and picked up 31 and six wickets, respectively.
Article Summary: Mohit Sharma set to join Chennai Super Kings support staff as bowling coach. The 38-year-old has played 120 fixtures in the IPL and has 134 wickets to his name. The Haryana bowler announced his retirement from professional cricket in December.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi backs Gen Z protests: 'Stop punishing women for crimes against them'
Article Text:
"Stop punishing women for the crimes committed against them," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday backed the ongoing student-led protests over women’s safety, accusing the government of responding to violence against women by restricting their movement instead of making public spaces safer.His remarks came amid renewed protests in Delhi following the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in south Delhi. Hundreds of students, many of them women, have taken to the streets over the past week demanding safer public spaces, stronger policing and greater accountability."Stop punishing women for the crimes committed against them," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X."Across our country, women are afraid to walk the streets, afraid of being harassed, afraid of being raped. And the government’s answer: stay at home," he said.Rahul Gandhi argued that asking women to restrict their movement amounted to victim-blaming instead of addressing the conditions that make public spaces unsafe."This is patriarchy at work: a system that blames the victim and shields the criminal. It is time to smash it," he said.The Congress leader said the focus should instead be on making streets safer, challenging attitudes that enable violence against women and ensuring swift punishment for offenders."The solution is not to lock women inside. It is to make our streets safe, to confront the mindset of men who mistreat women, and to punish those who attack them, swiftly and without exception," the Congress leader said.Protests over the Aastha Kunj case have grown across Delhi University. Students from institutions including Lady Shri Ram College, Miranda House, Gargi College and BR Ambedkar University have participated in demonstrations, raising concerns over harassment, poorly lit streets and restrictions imposed on women because of safety fears.The issue has also reached the Supreme Court. On Monday, the court questioned the Delhi government and police over recent crimes against women and girls in the national capital and sought accountability over what it described as failures in ensuring public safety.Rahul Gandhi urged more young people, particularly women from Gen Z, to join peaceful protests."Thousands of students and young people are on the streets demanding safety for women. I urge even more young women, especially GenZ across India to come out in stronger numbers," he said."This government is deaf to your pain and will only listen when it’s under pressure. Peaceful protest is your democratic right, and I stand with you wholeheartedly," he added.Creative placards and slogans such as "Abort Patriarchy", "My favourite season is FALL of patriarchy", "Bas bohot ho gaya" (enough is enough), and "Bade bade shehron mein aisi chhoti soch nahi chalegi" (such a narrow mindset will not work in big cities) stood out as protesters marched through the campus amid heavy police presence.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses government of responding to violence against women by restricting their movement. His remarks come amid renewed protests in Delhi following the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl. Hundreds of students, many of them women, have taken to the streets over the past week.

Article Title: Punjab's election drug debate has old players in new roles: BJP, Congress attack as AAP defends its record
Article Text:
Punjab’s drug debate returns ahead of 2027

"The sarpanch is also responsible for my death. I had questioned Cheema about drugs. My son takes drugs. My house was sold. I don't have anything and finally now I have consumed poison.

The problem of drugs has not been solved anywhere in Punjab."

BJP takes the drug battle on the road

BJP leader Anurag Thakur said the state has to be made 'Aam Aadmi Party Mukt' for turning it into 'Nasha Mukt'

From four weeks to three months: Punjab's many deadlines

Congress, SAD join the attack

Punjab finance minister blamed BJP-SAD for the drug menace in the state,

Channi hits out at AAP govt

Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal has appealed to women in Punjab to unite and launch an 'andolan'

AAP hits back: What about the years before 2022?

Beyond the blame game, what do numbers say

Punjab has seen this cycle before

NEW DELHI:Those were among the last recorded words of Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old Dalit man from Dirba in Sangrur district, before his death. His family alleged that he had been pushed to the edge after questioning Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema about the easy availability of drugs in the area.Gulzar died, but his words reverberated across poll-bound Punjab. The BJP, Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal trained their guns on the Bhagwant Mann government, accusing it of failing to control the drug menace. AAP hit back, questioning their own records in power.Drugs have shadowed election after election in the state. Captain Amarinder Singh went into the 2017 polls promising to break the backbone of the drug trade within four weeks. Five years later, AAP sought votes with its own promise of eliminating the menace within months.Now, with Punjab headed for another assembly election in 2027, drugs are again moving to the centre of the conversation.Only the roles have changed.AAP, which once attacked Congress and the SAD-BJP government from the outside, now has nearly five years in office to defend. Congress wants to use AAP's old promises against it. And the BJP, still trying to expand its footprint in Punjab, has launched perhaps its biggest statewide campaign yet around the issue.Leading the opposition charge is the BJP, which has the weakest presence in the state as of now, but is making the strongest pitch for power.The Punjab BJP, on September 18, launched its 13-day 'Nasha Mukt Yatra' to turn its anti-drug campaign into a statewide political roadshow ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. The party divided its campaign into four yatras covering nearly 4,000 km and all 117 assembly constituencies.The campaign will end on September 30, with Union home minister Amit Shah likely to address the concluding rally. All the top BJP leaders including Union ministers and party chief ministers from other states have joined the campaign against drugs in Punjab.Yet the BJP has a political history to answer for too. For 10 years, from 2007 to 2017, it shared power with the Shiromani Akali Dal, the period AAP repeatedly points to whenever its record on drugs is questioned.Ahead of the 2017 election, Amarinder Singh's four-week promise became one of the defining messages of the Congress campaign. He later clarified that his pledge was about breaking the backbone of the drug supply chain rather than completely eliminating every trace of drugs within a month.By 2022, the roles had changed. AAP was the challenger and Arvind Kejriwal and other party leaders promised quick action, speaking of tackling the menace within three to four months of forming the government.The BJP has done its homework well. It knows that the drug menace in Punjab is deep-rooted and hence has sought a timeframe of two years to eradicate it. However, Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has claimed that the BJP will destroy and eliminate the entire drug network within six months if voted to power in the state.Therein lies Punjab's problem: Congress cannot remind AAP about its three-month promise without being reminded of its own four-week vow. BJP cannot attack AAP without being taken back to its decade in government with SAD.Almost every party pointing fingers today has a past of its own to explain.The Congress narrative on the drug menace seems to have been lost in the face of BJP’s high-decibel anti-drug campaign. The party, which for a long time was struggling to set its own house in order amid infighting, has done little till now to capitalise on the alleged failures of the AAP government to tackle the drug menace.The first big Congress show on the ground was only after Sachin Pilot took charge as state incharge and managed to get the rival state unit factions on one stage to protest against Punjab minister Cheema over the suicide of Gulzar.Pilot said: “If someone raises their voice against drugs, they face such attacks. I believe the government can go to any extent to suppress and conceal these voices. There are two sets of laws in the country, one for ministers and another for the common man. This cannot go on. I feel the government is completely on the back foot regarding the issue of drugs.”He then turned to AAP's pre-2022 promise: “The Aam Aadmi Party had promised in Punjab that they would eliminate the drug menace within three months of forming the government. They stand completely exposed. I sense a stir for change in Punjab, and change will happen.”Leader of opposition Partap Singh Bajwa has blamed both the AAP-led state government and the BJP-led Union government for turning the state's drug crisis into a political blame game instead of dismantling the drug supply chain.“Bhagwant Mann cannot wash his hands of responsibility by talking about cross-border, the BSF and Mundra Port. At the same time, the BJP cannot absolve itself by blaming Punjab while the international border, ports and the national drug-trafficking network fall within areas where the Union government has a critical responsibility. Punjab's youth need action, not a Mann-Modi blame-game,” Bajwa said.The Congress challenge is daunting. While on the one hand it has to target the AAP government’s failures, on the other, it also has to prevent the BJP from running away with the anti-drug fight initiative.SAD faces much the same problem. Bikram Singh Majithia recently took a jibe at the Punjab government when he said: “Under AAP's regime, delivery of drugs is faster than that of food.”Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal has also appealed to women in Punjab to unite and launch an ‘andolan’ to free the state from the drug menace, including through ‘thikri pehra’, a community policing practice in which people guard their localities during emergencies.AAP's response is to ask its rivals to look backwards before judging the Mann government.Punjab minister Cheema, who is at the centre of the row over Gulzar’s suicide, shifted the blame to the BJP and the SAD.“The BJP should look at its own record. The drug menace intensified during the 10 years of the SAD-BJP government from 2007 to 2017. It was during that period that terms such as 'chitta' and 'smack' became widely associated with Punjab, with countless young lives being destroyed by addiction,” Cheema said.Countering the BJP offensive, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has alleged that the majority of narcotics entering the country originate from Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled states and major maritime entry points controlled by the Centre.Kejriwal alleged: “Today, 80% of the drugs are coming from BJP-ruled states - Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, UP, Delhi. Has the BJP failed to stop the drug trade in its own states, or does it not want to stop it? Their government has been in power in Gujarat for thirty years, and the highest drug trade is there. Drugs enter India through Mundra Port, and stopping that is the responsibility of the central BJP government.”Bhagwant Mann, meanwhile, has launched the ‘Soorma’ campaign to honour drug-rehabilitated people with specially crafted ‘Soorma’ rings and T-shirts. The chief minister said the initiative aimed to transform recovered drug victims into “Ambassadors of Hope”, who will lead the fight against addiction at the grassroots.The Mann government has numbers with which to defend itself.Punjab Police says its ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’ campaign has resulted in tens of thousands of cases and arrests. More recent state figures put the tally since March 2025 at 61,824 FIRs, 81,433 arrests and 3,918 kg of heroin seized.AAP presents the numbers as evidence that the state machinery is finally going hard after the networks. Its opponents turn the argument around: if such large quantities are still being seized and so many people are still being arrested, how deeply rooted does the trade remain?High seizures can show a crackdown is working but they can also show the scale of the problem being confronted.The government says its strategy now goes beyond policing. It has expanded treatment and rehabilitation under ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’, with 547 OOAT centres, 219 de-addiction centres and 91 rehabilitation centres, besides programmes involving schools and local communities.For AAP, this forms the other half of its defence: the battle against drugs cannot be measured only through FIRs and seizures but also through treatment and rehabilitation.In 2017, anger over drugs was directed largely at the SAD-BJP government and Congress promised quick action. By 2022, Congress was on the defensive and AAP used the same issue to argue that Punjab's traditional parties had failed. In 2027, AAP is the incumbent being asked many of the questions it once asked others.The slogans have changed and the roles have reversed, but the question has survived different governments and different deadlines: after so many promises to make Punjab drug-free, why is the state heading into yet another election talking about the same problem?
Article Summary: Drugs have shadowed election after election in the state. The BJP, Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal trained their guns on the Bhagwant Mann government, accusing it of failing to control the drug menace. AAP, which once attacked Congress and the SAD-BJP government, now has nearly five years in office to defend.

Article Title: Government mulls steps to save rabi crops from drought
Article Text:
Centre gears up for weak rainfall, orders data-driven plan to safeguard rabi crops

NEW DELHI: Apprehending the possibility of deficient rainfall in the upcoming sowing season, Centre Monday discussed contingency measures to minimise its impact on rabi (winter-sown) crops, with Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan calling for data-driven planning, stronger Centre-state coordination, weekly crop monitoring, balanced fertiliser use and water budgeting.Amid indications that the kharif (summer-sown) crops' output may not match last year's level despite progress in acreage, the minister, while addressing farm scientists and policymakers at a national conference, also emphasised the need to drive the rabi strategy through less water-consuming pulses and oilseeds.The conference was convened to discuss the farm strategy, keeping in view the current drought situation in many states so that low moisture content in the soil and shortage of water for irrigation due to deficient rainfall do not impact farming significantly. The sowing of rabi crops such as wheat and mustard begins in Oct.Centre will send teams to Karnataka and Maharashtra to assess the drought situation. Nearly two-thirds of Maharashtra has been affected, and the state has already declared a drought, while Karnataka is also facing drought-like conditions due to a monsoon rainfall deficit of 30%.
Article Summary: Centre will send teams to Karnataka and Maharashtra to assess the drought situation. Nearly two-thirds of Maharashtra has been affected, and the state has already declared a drought. Karnataka is also facing drought-like conditions due to a monsoon rainfall deficit of 30%.

Article Title: Supreme Court: Will fix timeline for FSSAI to enforce front-of-pack labelling
Article Text:
SC rejects FSSAI’s FoPL timeline, says 365-day voluntary rollout unreasonable

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday refused to accept the timeline proposed by FSSAI for the implementation of front-of-pack labelling (FoPL) for food products, including four months' time for framing regulations and a 365-day voluntary implementation period for food businesses after notification, saying it was unreasonable and decided to fix the timeline for the food regulator.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, however, made it clear to the regulator that it has to implement the court's order, which is in the national interest, in true spirit and not delay implementation. It asked why the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had fixed such a long timeframe to implement it as consultations with stakeholders had taken place in 2022."Why voluntary compliance for a year?... Why do you want to start afresh with the exercise of hearing and calling for objections? You started in 2022, what did you do in the last four years?"SC also termed advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi's plea for immediate implementation of FoPL as unreasonable and said it would pass an order to fix all contentious issues.Additional solicitor general Brijender Chahar, appearing for FSSAI, said the process initiated in 2022 was relating to a star-rating system based on an entirely different criterion. The bench, however, said the issue involved was very important and there should not be any more delay."We appreciate your initiative but there is a lot which is required to be done to give meaningful effect to what we want to achieve," SC said.Reserving the order, SC told FSSAI, "Whatever order we now pass will be binding on you, and we expect you to implement it scrupulously. We are undertaking this entire exercise for the good of the nation and for the good of citizens. We will now pronounce the final order. And we will keep it after some time to report due compliance in each and every direction. Do not disappoint us on the day when the matter comes up for reporting compliance. "
Article Summary: SC rejects FSSAI’s FoPL timeline, says 365-day voluntary rollout unreasonable. Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran made it clear to the regulator that it has to implement the court's order in true spirit.

Article Title: On deadlines, we must also look within: Supreme Court
Article Text:
TMC MLAs’ disqualification plea: SC says judiciary must introspect before setting deadlines

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: On a petition seeking direction to West Bengal speaker to expeditiously decide the disqualification petitions against rebel TMC MLAs, SC Monday said before setting a deadline for other constitutional authorities, the judiciary must introspect whether it conformed to statutory deadlines for adjudication of cases.When senior advocate Kapil Sibal pressed for seeking a response from the office of the speaker on the three-month-old disqualification petitions, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it will dispose of the petition asking the Supreme Court to abide by its 2020 judgement in Keisham Meghachandra Singh case, fixing a three-month deadline for a decision by the speaker.Sibal said he had no problem with this order but requested the court to examine the set pattern in which speakers delay a decision on disqualification petitions placing a premium to defections.Justice Bagchi said, "We should hold the mirror to ourselves before giving directions. There are so many statutes that require the judiciary to conclude proceedings within a timeframe. We are gloriously in breach of these."The disqualifications were filed on July 8 by TMC against 10 rebel MLAs who formed a separate block.The three-month time period for the speaker to decide the disqualification petitions ends on Oct 8.The CJI-headed bench said, "We have every reason to believe that the speaker of the legislative assembly is fully cognisant of the principles stated in the Keisham Meghachandra Singh ruling and will make all endeavour to take an appropriate decision within that framework."
Article Summary: SC says judiciary must introspect before setting deadlines for other constitutional authorities. The disqualifications were filed on July 8 by TMC against 10 rebel MLAs who formed a separate block. The three-month time period for the speaker to decide the disqualification petitions ends on Oct 8.

Article Title: Won't reopen Sohrabuddin case but will test validity of acquittal of all accused: SC
Article Text:
2005 Sohrabuddin encounter case: SC to test acquittals by trial court, Bombay HC

NEW DELHI: SC Monday agreed to test the validity of acquittal of police officers and all other accused concurrently by the trial court and Bombay high court in the controversial 2005 Sohrabuddin fake encounter case.Appearing for petitioner Rubabuddin Sheikh, brother of Sohrabuddin, senior advocate D Seshadri Naidu told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that his client lost his brother, sister-in-law and brother's friend Tulsiram Prajapati yet the trial court and the HC overlooked critical evidence to acquit all 22 accused, 21 of them police officers from Gujarat, Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh.The CJI-led bench said it would not reopen the case relating to fake encounter killings of Sohrabuddin, who had multiple criminal cases pending against him, or Prajapati, but would examine the strength of testimonies of witnesses.Appearing for some of the acquitted accused, senior advocate K Parameshwar told the bench that HC, in its appellate capacity, had considered the testimony of each of the witnesses before approving the acquittals.The bench asked the CBI and the petitioner to flag important witnesses and their depositions to the SC on the next date of hearing while seeking responses from the acquitted accused to the appeal filed by Rubabuddin.Justice Bagchi said, "It is worrisome that there has been wholesale turning hostile of witnesses. More worrisome is the fact that those who had recorded their statements before the magistrate under Section 164 of Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), they also turned hostile."The petitioner said the high court had failed to discharge its appellate function especially when it was informed in no uncertain terms that the evidence was tainted because of a "tailored investigation" which was aggravated by the actions of an "unprincipled prosecutor".Sohrabuddin and his wife Kauser Bi, along with Prajapati, were allegedly abducted by a team of Gujarat and Rajasthan police in Oct 2005. While Prajapati was allowed to go, Sohrabuddin was killed in a fake encounter, and his wife was allegedly murdered. Prajapati was killed in another fake encounter a year later.
Article Summary: SC to test validity of acquittals by trial court, Bombay HC in 2005 Sohrabuddin fake encounter case. Article Title: Did Troy Aikman disagree with Ben Johnson’s call? The Chicago Bears coach faces scrutiny after costly 4th-down gamble
Article Text:
Did Troy Aikman disagree with Ben Johnson’s call? The Chicago Bears coach faces scrutiny after costly 4th-down gamble(Getty)

Troy Aikman wanted Chicago to take the points

Ben Johnson explains why he trusted the call

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Troy Aikman questioned Ben Johnson’s fourth-down decision during the Chicago Bears’ Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Chicago had a chance to add points after recovering a fumble deep in Philadelphia territory, but Johnson kept the offense on the field.The call failed, and Aikman made his preference clear on the Monday Night Football broadcast. Johnson later explained why he trusted the play instead of taking the field goal.The Bears recovered a fumble at the Eagles’ 15-yard line and reached first-and-goal from the 6. Rome Odunze then dropped a wide-open touchdown chance on third down before Chicago faced fourth-and-goal from the 3.Johnson stayed aggressive. The fourth-down pass fell incomplete, ending the possession without points.“I think Ben Johnson got a little too enamored about what he is capable of calling,” Aikman said during ESPN’s Monday Night Football broadcast. He then added, “I’d take the points.”That was the heart of Aikman’s criticism. Chicago had already forced a turnover and moved into prime scoring territory. A field goal would have guaranteed points, while the fourth-down call left the Bears with nothing.The missed chance became more noticeable when Jalen Hurts scored on a tush push before halftime.Philadelphia went into the break trailing 10-7.There was another factor surrounding Chicago’s offense. Caleb Williams missed the game with a hamstring injury, while Case Keenum started at quarterback. The Bears entered the matchup already adjusting their offense around the veteran backup.Johnson did not describe the decision as a random gamble after the game. His explanation focused on his confidence in the play and his discomfort with kicking from that position.“Where we were on that field, I didn’t feel great going that direction, kicking it,” Johnson said during his postgame press conference. “It just is a gut feel sometimes on those things and how comfortable I am with the play calls.”The play was designed for tight end Colston Loveland. Johnson’s comments show that he had already made his choice based on the situation and his belief in the call.Johnson also had plenty to like about the offense despite that failed possession. Chicago’s running game carried a major share of the workload, with both backs finishing with more than 100 rushing yards. Johnson said the Bears needed that ground attack to win the game.He also acknowledged one area where he could have done better as a play-caller. Johnson said he looked at the offense’s 36 rushing attempts and felt he probably called too many pass plays given how well the running game was working.That adds another layer to the Aikman criticism. The Bears coach was not simply chasing points. He was making decisions based on his confidence in specific plays and the way the game was developing.Aikman wanted the safer scoring option. Johnson trusted his call. The fourth-down miss gave the ESPN analyst a clear reason to question the choice, even as the Bears ultimately won the game 31-20.
Article Summary: Troy Aikman questioned Ben Johnson’s fourth-down decision during the Chicago Bears’ Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Chicago had a chance to add points after recovering a fumble deep in Philadelphia territory, but Johnson kept the offense on the field. Johnson later explained why he trusted the play instead of taking the field goal.

Thiruvananthapuram: West Indies were comfortably placed at 107 for no loss when Kuldeep Yadav was brought into the attack in the 16th over. Fourteen balls into his spell, West Indies opener John Campbell top-edged a tossed-up delivery to short fine leg, giving India the breakthrough they needed.Virat Kohli and Shubman Gill would later soak in the applause for their batting. But it was Kuldeep who helped India turn the game around at the Greenfield International Stadium with flight, dip and guile.Kuldeep is a rhythm bowler. In his nine-year international career, whenever he hits his stride early, he reaps dividends. Sunday was a case in point. Kuldeep showcased his full repertoire, from the tossed-up delivery above the batter’s eyeline and the wrong one to the quickish fuller delivery. He displayed all his wares to finish with 4/40 and win the Player of the Match award.“Personally, I liked my rhythm. Just varying the pace and trying to read the batters, where they are going to hit me,” Kuldeep said after India’s eight-wicket win.“Sometimes to get that confidence back you need to have a spell like this,” the 31-year-old added.For a man with Kuldeep’s skill set, it is baffling why he gets so little match time.Since his debut in 2017, Kuldeep has taken 198 wickets in this format at an average of nearly 27. Of the 10 ODIs and 28 T20Is India have played this year, he has featured in five and four games respectively.Even Kuldeep’s long-form career has been a start-stop affair, featuring sporadically in 19 Tests since his debut against Australia in Dharamshala in 2017.“Kuldeep needs to be handled with care and used as a wicket-taking bowler. The more he bowls, the better he gets because it will help him get into rhythm. We were surprised that Kuldeep has been benched for so many games. Article Title: ‘Nothing has changed’: Rohit Sharma opens up on his special bond with Virat Kohli

NEW DELHI: Rohit Sharma has opened up on his long-standing bond with Virat Kohli , describing a relationship built on camaraderie, mutual respect and a shared commitment to the Indian cause, while insisting that little has changed between the two despite their evolving roles.Rohit Sharma, speaking to JioStar ahead of India's second ODI against West Indies on Wednesday, shared his thoughts on his relationship with Kohli and revealed how the two continue to exchange ideas about their batting and the team's goals.The pair have been teammates for almost two decades, with Rohit making his India debut in 2007 and Kohli following a year later. From sharing the dressing room to leading India at different stages, their careers have been closely intertwined.“I think we were together. This started, I think, when we were playing in Australia, or right after Australia when we came to India. That's when this started, and whenever this plays on TV, we look at each other and laugh. Which is good, it's fun. People want masala, so there you go, there is some masala,” Rohit said.Rohit said the different personalities and methods of the two batters have never affected their shared objective.“Both of us, we've almost started playing at the same time. I made my debut in 2007, he made his debut in 2008. And since then, we've been trying to give our best for the team. So yeah, there's a strong camaraderie between the two of us,” he said.“We understand what it requires to be at a certain level when you're playing at this level. Methods are different, obviously, but that's how it should be, every individual is different.”Rohit was also emphatic about Kohli's contribution to Indian cricket and what he expects from his former captain going forward.“For what he has done for the team, for this team, there is no question, there is no asking what has he done. It's there for everyone to see it,” Rohit said.“And what he is going to do from here on now, I don't think anything has changed. He'll be the same Kohli that we know of: wants to come, prepare well, go get the runs, win games for Team India.”Rohit added that the same team-first approach remained evident irrespective of who was leading India.“When he was captain, pretty much the same. When I was captain, pretty much the same. And I don't see any reason why anything needs to change,” he said.Rohit also revealed that the two continue to have conversations about their individual games, with their mutual appreciation extending beyond their performances on the field.“Appreciation, appreciation if something good has happened, it has always been there from both sides. I appreciate what he has done, you know, when he took over as a captain with the Test team, especially. It was brilliant, what he did with that team,” Rohit said.“At the same time, there has been a lot of discussion about how both of us as individuals can improve our own game. So, sometimes if something is happening with my batting, he comes and mentions it, sometimes I mention it.”On the upcoming World Cup, Rohit said there was no need for him to explain its importance to Kohli, who has already played four 50-over World Cups.“No, no. He has been playing for so many years. Whether it's the '27 World Cup or the '23 World Cup, there's no need to explain it to him. World Cup is World Cup,” Rohit said.The two may now spend less time together away from cricket, but Rohit said their connection remains unchanged.“Now both of us are spending more time at home, which is always nice,” he said.(Watch Rohit Sharma’s exclusive interview on JioHotstar and Star Sports Network, September 30)(Watch the ICC Men’s ODI World Cup schedule announcement on JioHotstar and Star Sports, October 1)

China’s Sun Yunong finished second with 26, while Kuwait’s Hajar Abdulmalik took bronze with 21.Dhanda’s 28 also shattered the previous Asian record of 24. The Indian had already announced her intent by topping qualification with 118 hits out of 125, and she carried that form into the six-shooter final to produce the biggest result of her career in the process delivering India its first individual gold medal of the 2026 Games and taking the country’s tally to five gold medals and 47 overall.Earlier in the day, Dhanda had already played a central role in India’s women’s trap team silver, joining Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer to finish second behind China.For Dhanda, the triumph comes just months after she broke new ground at the ISSF World Cup in Lonato, Italy. In July, she became the first Indian woman to win an individual gold medal in trap at an ISSF World Cup.The Asian Games gold now gives that World Cup success a continental dimension.Dhanda had arrived in Aichi-Nagoya as the reigning Asian champion, having won gold at the 2025 Asian Shooting Championships. She also had a mixed-team bronze from the ISSF World Cup in Almaty earlier this year.Dhanda was inspired to take up shooting after watching her maternal cousin Lakshay Sheoran win a silver medal in men's trap at the 2018 Asian Games. Sheoran also lent her his gun when she was beginning her journey in the sport. Years later, Dhanda has followed him to the Asian Games podium, but has gone one better by winning gold.The rise has been backed by the Indian Army, where Dhanda serves as a Naib Subedar in the Corps of Military Police. She trains at the Army Marksmanship Unit in Mhow and works with foreign coach Peter Wilson, the London 2012 Olympic trap champion. Article Title: From Jamshedpur slum to Asian Games: Joga Purty’s unlikely climb to India’s speed climbing record
Article Text:
Joga Purty during a practice session and (pic right) with her coach Bibhas

Kolkata:

When Joga Purty first walked into the climbing wall at JRD Tata Sports Complex in Jamshedpur, she had no idea what sport climbing was.A friend had suggested she tag along, and curiosity brought her there. Nearly seven years later, the 19-year-old from a modest family in Jamshedpur is India’s national record holder in speed climbing and on her way to the Asian Games “I never thought I would get an opportunity to compete at the Asian Games,” said Purty, who will make her debut in women’s speed climbing at the continental showpiece in Japan on Tuesday.“To be honest, my reaction was quite normal. I didn’t know much about the Games then, and I had already travelled for international competitions, so I didn’t think of it as something very different.”The Asiad may be her biggest stage yet, but the teenager’s journey has been anything but straightforward.Her father, Nandu, runs a small shop while her mother, Jhana, works as a domestic help. The youngest among three siblings, it was initially difficult for Purty to convince her family and neighbours that climbing was worth pursuing.“Joga comes from a humble background and grew up in the slum area. In the early days, she would often miss training sessions. I used to visit her home and speak to her parents to convince them to let her come for practice,” said Bibhas Roy, who trained her at Tata Steel Adventure Foundation (TSAF) Climbing Academy before moving to Bengaluru as India’s national coach in 2024.But the turning point came when she won medals in all three climbing disciplines at a national championship before the Covid-19 pandemic. “When my photo appeared in the newspapers, my mother became very proud. After that, nobody questioned my participation anymore,” she recalled.Although Purty initially competed in all three disciplines of sport climbing — boulder, lead and speed — her coaches soon recognised where her true potential lay. “Once we realised she was excelling in speed climbing, we decided to focus entirely on that discipline,” Roy said.The move quickly brought results. Purty announced herself on the international stage by winning a silver medal at 2024 IFSC Asian Youth Climbing Championships.Since then, she has represented India at World Championships and 2026 Asian Climbing Championships, while repeatedly lowering her own national record. Her current national mark of 7.37 seconds sealed her place in India’s Asian Games squad.Ahead of the Asian Games, Purty spent two months training in Indonesia before attending a camp in Thailand. While Roy admits Purty’s timings did not improve as much as expected during the latest overseas stint, he remains convinced that her best days lie ahead.“Her biggest strengths are her natural power and explosive speed. If she continues training properly and remains disciplined, I believe she can break into the six-second range within the next year,” he said.Climbing is also an expensive sport and for Purty, support from the Tata Steel Adventure Foundation has played a key role in keeping her climbing dream alive. A good pair of climbing shoes costs around Rs 10,000 and typically lasts only three to six months depending on usage. A harness can cost upwards of Rs 11,000, while chalk bags and chalk powder add significantly to the expenses.Competition at the Asian Games, however, will be fierce, with climbers from Kazakhstan, Indonesia, China and hosts Japan among the favourites. Yet Roy believes his protégé has the qualities required to compete with the continent’s best.“She has a very bright future and the potential to qualify for the Olympics one day,” he said.
Article Summary: Joga Purty will make her debut in women’s speed climbing at the continental showpiece in Japan on Tuesday. The 19-year-old from a modest family in Jamshedpur is India's national record holder in speed climbing and on her way to the Asian Games. Her father, Nandu, runs a small shop while her mother, Jhana, works as a domestic help.

Article Title: Savitha Shri’s Chess Olympiad gold demands a closer look beyond the stunning 9/10
Article Text:
Savitha Shri in Round 10 of Chess Olympiad (Photo by Michal Walusza for FIDE)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Savitha Shri’s individual gold medal performance (9 points in 10 games) is a highly notable achievement. Her exploits at the Chess Olympiad that concluded in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on Sunday, however, warrant a closer look.“I really don't know what to say... for gambling the positions or keeping us tense throughout the rounds! But yes, when there were really tense moments, she was strong enough to capitalise on those opportunities. She has the fighting spirit and she is not scared of playing any position. Irrespective of the evaluation, she keeps fighting,” India’s top board player Koneru Humpy told the Chessbase India webcast about Savitha Shri.In other words, those were not simply clean wins where she outplayed her opponents. The majority of the games featured multiple inaccuracies, which is the norm in shorter time controls but not in classical chess.Veteran GM Levon Aronian told Lichess in an interview that if players want to win, they will have to take gambles these days as the level of preparation has increased. There is, however, a thin line between taking risks and being in reasonable control despite taking liberties.It is also unclear if Savitha Shri was fully aware of the dangers of her inaccuracies. Savitha Shri, 19, also played on the reserve board (fifth). Despite slipping from the Elo high of 2435 four years ago to 2382 at this Olympiad, all her rivals were lower-rated than her.Still, the value of IM Savitha Shri’s performance for India cannot be ignored. She scored eight wins when GMs K Humpy, R Vaishali and Divya Deshmukh scored a combined nine wins.Vaishali (2.5/6) was rested for four of the last seven rounds. Her form is a huge worry as she is expected to challenge China’s Ju Wenjun for the women’s world crown early next year.

Article Title: Rain ruins India’s Asian Games cricket quarterfinal, fans left with ‘far-off view’ of players
Article Text:
India's Abhishek Sharma meets Afghanistan's team members (PTI Photo)

Nisshin: Handshakes between the teams. That was the only action possible at the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin on Monday as persistent rain forced both Asian Games cricket quarterfinals to be abandoned without a ball being bowled.Despite most of the outfield being covered, the surface remained wet and, with no sign of the sun, officials had little option but to call off the matches before the toss.India and Pakistan advanced to their respective semifinals by virtue of being the higher-ranked teams. For the sizable number of Indian fans who had travelled from different parts of Japan hoping to watch their team in action, it was a major disappointment.Rahil Yadav, who lives in Kyoto, said he had taken a chance despite the weather.“Given the weather for the past few days, I knew it was unlikely that the match would happen, but I was just being hopeful because for us Indians living here, it was a great opportunity to watch our team in action. It was hard to get things up and running here. That said, there is nothing we can do and weather is a big part of cricket. The rain is a bit unseasonable because in Sept last year it was warm and sunny. The typhoons usually blow over and we hoped the weather would hold up. We have lost three matches in a row now. We can only hope for the weather to get better,” the Englishman said.India’s semifinal opponent will depend on the outcome of the Nepal-Sri Lanka quarterfinal, scheduled for Tuesday. If that match goes ahead, India will face the winner on Thursday. Should it be washed out, Sri Lanka will advance on the basis of their higher ranking.Before the team left for the venue, they were greeted by Indian Olympic Association president and athletics legend PT Usha at the hotel.

Article Title: Trapped hand, speeding SUV and desperate climb: How cops stopped gutka-laden vehicle
Article Text:
Head constable, M Velmurugan, claimed that the chase started at Vilankurichi and he clung on to the SUV till Karumathampatti, which is about 40km away.

,





COIMBATORE: A police head constable foiled an attempt by three smugglers to escape in a gutka-laden sports utility vehicle, by clinging to the top of the vehicle on Avinashi Road till a highway patrol team intercepted the gang at Karumathampatti near here on Sunday morning.Head constable, M Velmurugan, claimed that the chase started at Vilankurichi and he clung on to the SUV till Karumathampatti, which is about 40km away. The three smugglers have been arrested.Acting on a tip-off, a police team led by Kovilpalayam sub-inspector Vignesh and head constable Velmurugan attempted to stop the SUV (KA 05 NG 7692) at Vilankurchi near Kovilapalayam around 5.45am.Velmurugan climbed atop the SUV when the driver slowed the vehicle but refused to halt and sped towards Avinashi. The constable clung atop the SUV by holding the roof rails of the vehicle despite the smugglers driving the vehicle athigh speed.Vignesh immediately informed the Karumathampatti police and highway patrol team on Avinashi Road, who chased the vehicle for nearly an hour and eventually intercepted it at Karumathampatti and saved Velmurugan without any injuries.Police found more than 100kg of gutka products in the car and identified three smugglers travelling in the car as P Babu Dhara, 27, A Rajesh, 23 and S Suresh, 20, all from Rajasthan.They were smuggling the contraband from Karnataka to Coimbatore. Police seized the contraband and the car.Meanwhile, prohibition and excise minister K Vignesh and minister for backward classes welfare RS Rajakannappan spoke to Velmurugan over a video call and congratulated him for his bravery.They said they would take Velmurugan’s daring act to the attention of chief minister C Joseph Vijay.Later, Velmurugan told TOI“When we approached the vehicle, the driver stopped and rolled down the window. While we were questioning the occupants, he started moving the car and closed the window, trapping the SI’s hand inside. Our SI ran for a few metres with his hand trapped inside. Luckily, the SI fell on the road without any injuries, but I climbed atop the SUV. I realised the suspects should not be allowed to escape, so I held on to the rails tightly till they were captured. As police personnel, we were just doing our duty.”
Article Summary: Head constable, M Velmurugan, claimed that the chase started at Vilankurichi and he clung on to the SUV till Karumathampatti, which is about 40km away. The three smugglers have been arrested. Police seized the contraband and the car.

The TikTok video that changed everything

Her advice to content creators

Shereen Pavlides did not plan to become a social media star. The Garnet Valley High School Class of 1990 graduate and former Glen Mills resident built her career around food over several years, moving from restaurant work and private mortgage insurance to culinary school, food writing and television. Today, millions of people follow her cooking content online.Pavlides is known online as Cooking With Shereen. She has built a following of about 5 million on TikTok, more than 2 million on Facebook, over 1 million on Instagram and roughly 1.45 million YouTube subscribers. Her online audience grew as she shared simple recipes and cooking techniques from her own kitchen.According to Delco Today, Pavlides' journey into food began early. As a teenager, Pavlides worked in restaurants. She later spent years in private mortgage insurance before enrolling in culinary school in New York City. That decision changed the direction of her career and led her into several food-related roles.After culinary school, Pavlides worked in food styling, food writing and recipe development. She also worked in test kitchens, including at Good Housekeeping. Her experience eventually took her to QVC, where she became an on-air guest and appeared in more than 186 live broadcasts demonstrating cookware, bakeware and kitchen appliances.Her television work played an important role in what came next. Viewers regularly asked Pavlides for her recipes, and those requests encouraged her to create content of her own.She launched her YouTube channel in 2019 and began experimenting with TikTok soon after. One of the videos that helped her gain attention was her fifth TikTok video. It was simple tutorial on making chicken cutlets. The video received millions of views and helped establish her he simple, from-scratch cooking style that became synonymous to Pavlides' online content.Pavlides continued developing recipes and filming them in her own kitchen. She also remains involved in editing her videos even as her audience grew.Her work now takes an estimated 60 to 80 hours a week. Even with a large online following, she continues to develop her own recipes and remain involved in the production of her content.The social media career has also taken Pavlides beyond online platforms. She has appeared on major television programmes and published two bestselling cookbooks. She is currently working on a third cookbook. At the same time, Pavlides is planning to expand her production team as her work continues to grow.Her career has moved from working in restaurants and food-related jobs to creating content that reaches millions of people through several platforms. However, the path has not been limited to one type of food media. Her experience in food styling, writing, recipe development, test kitchens and live television has all become part of the career she has built around her online presence.Pavlides has also shared advice for people who want to build their own careers in content creation. Speaking to aspiring creators at a recent Broadcast Pioneers event, she said creators should focus on providing something useful to their audiences.“Don’t make it about yourself. Give something that can help somebody else and be useful in their lives. Quality of your content really matters, because you are building trust,” Pavlides said.She also stresses on the importance of having a direct relationship with an audience and being genuine in the way content is presented.“Talk to your audience, not at them, and be your authentic self,” she said. “Be good at what you’re communicating and let the rest ride,” Pavlides added.What began with a YouTube channel in 2019 and early experiments on TikTok has since become Cooking With Shereen, with a large audience spread across TikTok, Facebook, Instagram and YouTube.

She has built a following of about 5 million on TikTok, more than 2 million on Facebook, over 1 million on Instagram and roughly 1.45 million YouTube subscribers. Even with a large online following, she continues to develop her own recipes and remain involved in the production of her content.

Article Title: 'Chilli powder in eyes': Fashion design graduate, sister ram scooter into Delhi delivery boy, rob him
Article Text:
A fashion design graduate and her Class 12 dropout sister were arrested for robbing a delivery boy in Rohini. (Photo credit: X)





NEW DELHI: A fashion design graduate and her Class 12 dropout sister were arrested for allegedly robbing a delivery boy in Rohini , police said.One of them posed as a customer and tried to snatch parcels from his delivery bag, while the other allegedly arrived on a scooty and struck him from behind.DCP (Rohini) Shashank Jaiswal said the incident took place around 7.20pm on Sept 25 near Hanuman mandir in Sector 5. One of the women allegedly approached the delivery boy posing as a customer and attempted to forcibly take parcels from his bag.When he resisted, she allegedly threw chilli powder into his eyes. Meanwhile, the second woman arrived on a scooty and allegedly struck him from behind, causing him to fall and sustain a leg injury. The two then fled with several parcels.“This is so far their first target. We are looking into whether they may have been involved in similar incidents earlier,” Jaiswal said.A case under sections 309(6) (voluntarily causing hurt while committing robbery) and 3(5) (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of BNS was registered at Budh Vihar police station.Following the incident, a team was formed to investigate the case.Police said technical surveillance and human intelligence helped identify the accused as Nancy Singh, 26, and Gracy Singh , 20, both residents of Karol Bagh. Police arrested the sisters within 15 hours of registering the case.Three robbed parcels, along with the mobile phone and scooty allegedly used in the offence, were recovered from their possession, police said. During interrogation, the accused allegedly disclosed their involvement in the case.Police said Nancy had completed a fashion design course but was unemployed, while Gracy was a Class 12 dropout. Further investigation is underway.
