NEW DELHI: Since becoming world champion two years ago, noise has followed Dommaraju Gukesh almost everywhere, at times making it feel as though he isn't worthy of the title he rightfully won.But on Friday, when India needed the youngest world champion in history to deliver a win, he did exactly that, turning around an almost-lost position to beat Germany's Alexander Donchenko in Round 9 of the 46th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.It was the kind of performance that felt like it could quiet the criticism all on its own.Playing black, Gukesh traded off his dark-squared bishop early to damage White's pawn structure, then spent the middlegame manoeuvring patiently, repositioning knights, expanding on the queenside with a5-a4, and probing for weaknesses without rushing.For a long stretch, the position stayed murky and roughly balanced, with both sides shuffling pieces and neither able to land a clean blow.It was in the run-up to the time control that things turned dangerous for Gukesh. Donchenko doubled his rooks on the e-file and pushed one all the way to e6, aiming squarely at Black's king, which had been forced to step out to f7 for safety.With his own clock running low, Gukesh had to defend precisely while trying to generate counterplay of his own on the kingside, pushing his h- and g-pawns forward to create complications.It was a position where one careless move could have ended the game in White's favour.Gukesh held his nerve. As the pawn storms and piece trades settled down, he found a route to activate his queen and knight while White's pieces drifted out of coordination.The Chennai-born grandmaster found an excellent move with 51...Nf4. The German sacked Gukesh's knight with 52.Rxf4, but Donchenko's bishop was thus left hanging on c3; Gukesh's queen swooped in to capture it, and from there it was a matter of technique.A check with his queen forced Donchenko's king into an impossible spot, and White resigned rather than play on a piece down with his king exposed.Elsewhere on the board, Nihal Sarin, playing white, spent much of his game in some turmoil against Frederik Svane but held firm for a draw.With Gukesh's win already banked, Praggnanandhaa and Arjun Erigaisi didn't need to force matters either, settling for draws against Vincent Keymer and Matthias Bluebaum, respectively. India closed out the match 2.5-1.5.With the win, India moved to 15 points, still one point behind hosts Uzbekistan, who beat the United States on Friday to stay in front.India's women's team also had a productive Friday, with Vantika Agrawal and Divya Deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match against Uzbekistan.Vantika, playing white against Nilufarkhon Imomkuzieva, picked up an early pawn with a sharp tactical sequence; a check with her queen forced Black's king to give up material before the middlegame had properly begun.She nursed that small material edge through a long, technical battle, trading down into a rook endgame where her extra pawn and more active king proved decisive.Pushing her kingside pawns forward in the closing stages, Vantika eventually broke through, and Imomkuzieva had no way to hold the position together.Divya Deshmukh's game against Gulrukhbegim Tokhirjonova was a far longer and more chaotic affair.Both sides grabbed material early. Tokhirjonova's knight snatched a pawn on b7 just as Divya's queen picked up a stray piece on d2, leaving the position roughly balanced but sharp.What followed was a marathon battle through the middlegame and into a complex rook, knight and bishop endgame, with both players navigating tricky technical positions deep into the game.Divya's technique held up better over the long haul, and after 73 hard-fought moves, Tokhirjonova had nothing left to stop Black's advancing king, resigning the position.Those two results were enough to see India through the match, keeping the team firmly in the mix for a medal.As things stand, India's women sit second in the standings on 15 points, behind an in-form Chinese side on 17.With two rounds left, India's hopes of gold now depend largely on whether China slip up, but on Friday's evidence, neither Indian team looks inclined to make things easy for anyone chasing them either.In the Open section, India face Uzbekistan 2, while the women’s team take on China in the penultimate round of the Chess Olympiad.
Article Summary: Dommaraju Gukesh turns around an almost-lost position to beat Germany's Alexander Donchenko in Round 9 of the 46th Chess Olympiad. India's women's team also had a productive Friday, with Vantika Agrawal and Divya Deshmukh both delivering important wins to seal the match.

Article Title: Gurgaon road rage: 4 men smash car window, then attack complainants outside police station
Article Text:
Four men allegedly got out of the SUV and tried to open his car door.





GURGAON: Four men allegedly intercepted a car and smashed its window on Thursday before attacking the complainant and two of his associates outside New Colony police station, where they had gone to lodge a complaint about the incident.The complainant, Gautam, a resident of Madanpuri, told police he was driving towards New Colony after taking a U-turn near Hari’s Bakery when a Scorpio N (HR26FG5726) overtook his car and forced him to stop.Four men allegedly got out of the SUV and tried to open his car door. When they failed, they allegedly smashed the window, and the broken glass hit Gautam’s face. He told police he suspected the men had come to rob him and were carrying illegal weapons.Gautam said he managed to drive away and called his friends Ravindra Kataria and Sandeep Dahiya. The three then went to New Colony police station to lodge a complaint. Gautam told police that a dashcam in his car had recorded the incident.Police said an emergency response vehicle received information about the incident near Aryan Hospital in Sector 7. A team reached the spot and found Gautam, Ravindra and Sandeep there, but the Scorpio had left.Police later found the SUV parked near Sai Temple at New Colony turn. Gautam told police its occupants had entered a hotel opposite the spot. A police team went to the hotel and found three men — Ajay , Mohit and Piyush Bhardwaj — in room 105. Police said the three had consumed alcohol and took them into custody.A fourth man, identified as Shivam, was apprehended while allegedly fighting with Gautam and his friends near the police station.Police said that after getting out of the police vehicle, Mohit joined Shivam and allegedly attacked Gautam, Ravindra and Sandeep near the station gate. Police personnel intervened and all four accused were taken for medical examination at Sector 10 govt hospital.Ravindra and Sandeep were also medically examined. Their reports recorded five and two injuries, respectively. Gautam also alleged that Ravindra’s gold chain went missing during the assault and that the accused threatened to kill them if they encountered them elsewhere.An FIR was registered at New Colony police station under sections 115(2), 126(2), 324(4), 351(3), 3(5) and 72(C) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Article Summary: Four men allegedly intercepted a car and smashed its window on Thursday. They then allegedly attacked the complainant and two of his associates outside New Colony police station, where they had gone to lodge a complaint about the incident. The complainant, Gautam, a resident of Madanpuri, told police he suspected the men had come to rob him.

Article Title: In 2019, a Miami artist built a ceramic underwater reef to give coral a place to grip; her sculptures became a nursery-like habitat for reef animals instead of only gallery art
Article Text:
Artist Beatriz Chachamovits’ practice combines ceramics with marine research and education | instagram/@beatrizchachamovits

To Replenish With Water

Artist Beatriz Chachamovits’ practice combines ceramics with marine research and education | instagram/@beatrizchachamovits

The artwork was meant to change underwater

To Replenish With Water

Depth of Decision

Representative image of a coral reef, illustrating the underwater habitat that artist Beatriz Chachamovits sought to support through her ceramic reef sculptures | Wikimedia Commons

Her ceramics became part of a larger reef project

Modeling the Reef

To Replenish With Water

Beatriz Chachamovits is a Brazilian-born artist based in Miami who createdas an artificial reef for the Underwater Museum of Art off Florida's Gulf Coast. The work depicts bleached corals and sponges that are mixed with forms resembling plastic waste, with the expectation that living coral would eventually grow over its surface.The sculpture was part of the museum's 2019 installation, which placed 12 new artworks underwater near Grayton Beach State Park in South Walton, Florida. The Underwater Museum of Art was created in partnership with the South Walton Artificial Reef Association, and the sculptures were intended to serve a purpose beyond attracting divers. The organisations describe the museum as a way to create marine habitat while also providing cultural and educational opportunities.Chachamovits' piece was made to resemble several Florida coral species, including elkhorn, staghorn, brain and fire corals, as well as tube, vase and barrel sponges. The sculpture was primarily modelled from clay by making use of a 3D printer and then cast in clean white cement. The white surface was intentional, and represented coral bleaching at the starting point of the installation rather than trying to imitate a healthy, colourful reef.The Underwater Museum of Art says that the forms were designed to be covered over time by new and healthy corals, and the artificial object would gradually lose its original white appearance as organisms colonised the structure. That approach fits Chachamovits' wider work since her practice combines ceramics with marine research and education, and she has repeatedly used sculptures to represent coral bleaching, plastic pollution and changes to reef ecosystems. Her own account of the project says that she became interested in artificial reefs after creatingand has since focused on the structures as a way to provide surfaces where corals can attach and grow. Chachamovits describes artificial reefs as potential spaces where corals can attach, while reef animals can use the structures as habitat. The sculpture’s intended role was to provide a hard underwater structure that could be colonised over time. The Underwater Museum of Art sits in the Gulf of Mexico roughly a mile from shore, at a depth of about 58 feet, and divers need certification to visit the submerged works. The 2019 deployment added the work to a collection that already treated underwater sculpture as more than an art installation, and the museum's partnership with the artificial reef organisation meant that the pieces were selected and placed with marine habitat in mind. Chachamovits' sculpture was one of several works in that year's group, alongside structures such as, which is a series of concrete doorways designed with openings that could be used by marine life.Chachamovits continued developing work around the same idea after the 2019 installation, and her projects have included ceramic representations of endangered Florida reef species surrounded by objects such as bottles, cigarette butts, plastic caps and discarded toothbrushes. In those works, the waste is also made from ceramic rather than being actual marine debris.Through herproject, she has used sculpting activities to teach children about coral ecosystems. Her larger body of work examines the physical changes taking place on reefs through objects that can be seen and handled rather than through scientific charts alone. For, however, the most unusual part of the work remains its intended transformation, as the sculpture was placed underwater as a representation of a bleached reef, with the expectation that living organisms would eventually cover the manufactured surface and turn it into part of the surrounding marine habitat.
Article Summary: Beatriz Chachamovits is a Brazilian-born artist based in Miami. She created an artificial reef for the Underwater Museum of Art off Florida's Gulf Coast. The work depicts bleached corals and sponges mixed with forms resembling plastic waste, with the expectation that living coral would eventually grow over its surface. The sculpture’s intended role was to provide a hard underwater structure that could be colonised over time.

Article Title: Jassie Gill: I want to show Delhi Punjabis differently than they are usually shown as
Article Text:
'If I get a chance, I would love to go to Khan Market for kebabs. I would love to be around India Gate. That is the Delhi that I have seen in films,' says Jassie Gill

‘I only come to Delhi for shows or shooting, I would like to see more of the city’

‘Walking the ramp is still new for me’





Over the years, Delhi has become a home for singer and actor Jassie Gill , but he says that his love affair witah the city didn’t begin on a very good note. “I will always remember my first visit to Delhi. I had come to Rohini for a film promotion, and I had just started singing then. When I was on stage, ek dum se shor hua, Honey Singh aa gaya aur jo 10-15 log thay audience mein, woh bhi chale gaye. Toh bada dil toota uss din. That day, while returning, I told my friend that I felt very insulted and bad, and I would only be back in Delhi when people would invite me to perform. Otherwise aise Delhi nahin aaunga jab tak koi jaanega nahin,” Jassie shares after walking the ramp for Delhi Times Fashion Week as the showstopper.But now he is in Delhi almost every week for his performances. “Ab toh Delhi hamara apna hai. In the last 12 years, I have been coming here almost twice every week. Wedding season is about to begin, and 90% of our shows are in Delhi. Most of my songs get the highest views from Delhi and Jaipur,” he tells us.Jassie shares that though he visits the city often for work, he is still waiting to spend some leisure time here.He adds, “Since I only come here for shows or shooting, I mostly end up seeing the airport, hotels, and banquet halls (if performing at a wedding). If I get a chance, I would love to go to Khan Market for kebabs. I would love to be around India Gate. That is the Delhi that I have seen in films. I would love to shoot a movie or a music video here. ” Talking about the portrayal of Delhi Punjabis on screen, he shares, “I would want to show Delhi Punjabis a bit differently than what they are usually shown as. Films mein bahut dikhate hain ki woh daaru bahut peete hain, manchale hote hain, shararati hote hain. So I want to show that there are many other aspects to them too. We have so many good Punjabi artists; so many of them do sewa at gurdwaras. I would like to present this reality,” he says.The singer shares his experience from walking the ramp at Delhi Times Fashion Week, “I walked the ramp for the third time, and this is something that is still new for me. Whenever I am approached for any fashion show, I always try to be myself. I tell everyone that I should look like who I am in real life and would only wear something that I would want to own,” he said.
Article Summary: Singer and actor Jassie Gill shares his love affair with the city. He says he would love to spend more time in the city and see more of it. Gill says he wants to show Delhi Punjabis a bit differently than they are portrayed in films.

Article Title: Marching through the storm: ‘Hum Auratein Aazad Hain’ echoes across Delhi University
Article Text:
Women from various Delhi University colleges demonstrated for their freedom and safety against violence on Monday.





NEW DELHI: First came the slogans. Then came the rain. Umbrellas shot open across the crowd, handwritten placards were pulled closer and some students tried to shield their posters from the sudden downpour.But no one appeared to be going anywhere. If anything, the rain seemed to turn up the volume. "Hum leke rahenge aazadi," the women roared, their voices carrying through a rain-soaked North Campus as they continued walking.At 3pm Monday, Delhi University's Faculty of Arts became the starting point for another assertion by women that safety cannot come at the cost of their freedom. Under the banner 'Hum Auratein Aazad Hain', women from various colleges and members of the queer community gathered at Gate No. 7 before marching towards the Faculty of Arts gate opposite Daulat Ram College. The march eventually culminated at the Swami Vivekananda statue, where several women climbed onto the pedestal around it, placards held high as chants continued below.The march came days after the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in southeast Delhi sparked protests and renewed conversations around women's safety.Last week, women from several DU colleges had marched near Kamala Nehru College and LSR College, calling for safer streets, better lighting and accessible public transport, while opposing measures restricting women's movement after dark.Monday's demonstration came with a clear set of guidelines underlining that offensive language and sexist, misogynistic, casteist, homophobic or transphobic slurs, slogans or banners would not be tolerated. AI-generated posters and other media were also barred.On the road, the larger argument was told as much through cardboard and sketch pens as through speeches. 'Hum aazad hain sirf panno par', read one handwritten placard. A few steps away, another declared: 'Girls just wanna have fundamental rights.' There was anger, but also wit: 'Cutie nahi, kranti hoon.' Another poster turned the usual questions about women's whereabouts on their head: 'Beti ki location nahi, bete ka intent check karo. ' 'Mama raised a woman, not a coward,' said another.The chants carried the same argument. "Rapist ko andar karo, ladkiyon ko nahi," students shouted, rejecting restrictions on women as a response to sexual violence. Every few metres, another round of "aazadi" rose from the crowd, with voices from the back picking up where those at the front left off.For Sparshika, a Hansraj College student whose parents are in Dehradun, simply turning up was itself a decision. She said her parents did not want her to attend the demonstration despite it taking place during the day, citing safety concerns. "I cut the call and came," she said. "We want basic things like being able to move out freely. If I don't take this step now, my children will suffer even more."Her words reflected a recurring theme through the afternoon - why should a woman have to calculate the hour before deciding whether she can step outside?For Shefali, another DU student, the problem also lay in the questions routinely directed at women after incidents of violence. "I find it ridiculous when people link the safety of women to their clothes and timings. What about children who are attacked? What do they do to provoke someone?" she said.Though women remained at the centre of the march, a considerable number of men gathered along its periphery. Some walked at a distance, while others clapped and cheered as the slogans grew louder. Among them was Aryan, a Ramjas College student, who said changing attitudes among men was fundamental to addressing the problem. "The mindset of men needs to change. That's what is of fundamental importance," he said.Sahil, a student of Kirori Mal College, said the conversation needed to move away from asking women to rearrange their lives around unsafe conditions. "The problem needs to be dealt with from the core. Nobody should have to see the timing before stepping out. This is so basic and still, they have to agitate for it," he said.By the time the crowd reached Daulat Ram College, the rain had transformed the scene, but not the march. Clothes were soaked, handwritten posters had begun to curl at the edges and umbrellas jostled for space above the crowd. Some students squeezed beneath them, while others continued walking in the rain, drenched but still chanting.At the Swami Vivekananda statue, the march came to a halt, but the slogans did not. Several women climbed onto the pedestal around the statue, raising their placards above the crowd as others packed in below. Till the evening, the posters remained high and the chants continued, with the rain having done little to drown out the roar.
Article Summary: Women from various Delhi University colleges demonstrated for their freedom and safety against violence on Monday. The march came days after the gang rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park in southeast Delhi sparked protests and renewed conversations around women's safety.

Article Title: Ranbir Kapoor, Hema Malini, Sonam Kapoor join thousands to celebrate spiritual guru Rakeshji's 60th birthday
Article Text:
Ranbir Kapoor with spiritual guru Rakeshji





The 60th birthday celebrations of spiritual guru Gurudevshri Rakeshji, founder of Shrimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur (SRMD), were done in a grand style in Mumbai recently. Titled 'Aho Gurudev', the two-day gathering drew thousands of devotees from 23 countries, alongside spiritual leaders, noted industrialists, and prominent names from cinema and public life.Marking six decades of the founder's life, 60 new initiatives were announced for the benefit of a large section of society. Among the prominent names present at the celebration were Ranbir Kapoor Hema Malini , Sonam Kapoor, Sajid Nadiadwala and more.Soaking in the moment, Ranbir said he was left speechless on walking into the hall. "I have been in many places with large crowds, and you can sense the energy. Here it was very spiritual, very calm, full of love and smiling faces. That is very rare," he said, adding, "To see doctors travelling to the remotest parts of our country to help those in need is something that stands out to me in the mission's work. I think that is what true spirituality is. " Ranbir also highlighted that fatherhood and his portrayal of Lord Ram in the upcoming Ramayana brought him close to spirituality. On a lighter note, Ranbir added, "Even in a school, you can't get 30 children to listen to one teacher and follow. To see so many young people come together and believe in something shows it has touched them and made them more empathetic. I think Gurudevshri Rakeshji is a youth magnet!"Hema Malini, on her part, began her address with Sanskrit invocations and paid tribute to the guru-shishya tradition."A guru gives you the right path. When we are confused, it is the guru who holds our hand and takes us forward. At this event, we celebrate not merely 60 years of a life, but 60 years of light." Welcoming the mission's plan to open 60 Love and Care Centres, including one near Mathura, her constituency, the actor-politician thanked Gurudevshri and prayed for his long life and good health.Sonam Kapoor shared a personal experience and how spirituality is helping her post her pregnancy. She revealed that she had been practising sound healing with the mission's disciples through her recent pregnancy. "I am five months postpartum, and it really held my hand through some very difficult times."Meanwhile, filmmaker Subhash Ghai spoke of how one person's vision can transform so many people. "To me, Gurudevshri's work represents a different kind of spirituality - that of serving others," he said. Producer Sajid Nadiadwala said he was overwhelmed by the faith of devotees. On meeting Gurudevshri for the first time, he said, "It was a magical feeling. When anything is done without selfish reason, this is how people respond. "
Article Summary: The 60th birthday celebrations of spiritual guru Gurudevshri Rakeshji were done in a grand style in Mumbai. Among the prominent names present at the celebration were Ranbir Kapoor Hema Malini, Sonam Kapoor, Sajid Nadiadwala and more.

Article Title: LPG leak triggers blast at Sanpada snacks shop in Navi Mumbai, 2 injured
Article Text:
A LPG cylinder leakage caused a blast at a Sanpada snacks shop on Tuesday morning.





NAVI MUMBAI: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in sector-1, Sanpada on Tuesday morning. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.Purushottam Jadhav, Divisional officer of Vashi fire station said, "At 6.13 am, the Vashi fire station received the emergency call informing about a cylinder blast at a snacks shop in Pratik CHS on sector-1, Sanpada. The fire bridge team reached the spot within 5 minutes.It was found that the blast was due to leakage in one of the three LPG cylinders kept at snacks shop. The two men working at the snacks shop sustained severe burn injuries and were rushed to NMMC hospital, Vashi. Those injured were identified as Arjun Yadav (46) who has sustained 75 precent burn injuries and Manish Yadav (26), who has sustained 90 percent burns.The blast even caused damage to two shops adjacent to the snacks shop and three other shops in the neighbouring Abhimanyu CHS. While, the glass facade of Suraj hospital located opposite to Pratik CHS was shattered due to the impact of the blast."
Article Summary: Two men sustained severe burn injuries after a LPG cylinder leakage triggered a blast at a snacks shop on the ground floor of a society in Sanpada. The impact of the blast was so severe that the glass facade of a hospital, located about 50 feet away, was shattered. Fortunately, the patients and staff at the hospital were not hurt.

Article Title: 16 years after construction, KDMC mayor finally moves into civic bungalow
Article Text:
The bungalow was constructed in 2010.





KALYAN: Sixteen years after it was constructed, the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s (KDMC) new mayoral residence at Adharwadi finally got its first regular occupant, with mayor Harshali Chaudhari-Thavil performing the vastu shanti puja and entering the bungalow on Wednesday.The bungalow was constructed in 2010. However, a dispute over access to the property kept the residence largely unused for years. Several mayors subsequently attempted to resolve the road issue, but the efforts failed as villagers whose land was required for the access road were reportedly unwilling to part with the land.Even after the civic body spent lakhs of rupees on repairs, the bungalow remained unused. Former mayor Vinita Rane had performed a puja at the residence but chose not to stay there.With prolonged neglect, wooden furniture inside the bungalow was damaged and several portions were affected by termites. The civic administration later undertook extensive repairs to make the premises habitable again.After taking charge as mayor in February, Thavil took up the long-pending access issue. As she travels daily from Titwala to Kalyan, she personally held meetings with villagers and discussed their concerns. Following the resolution of the issues, the access road was finally constructed, paving the way for the mayoral residence to be used.After the road was made accessible and the neglected bungalow was completely repaired, Thavil finally entered the Adharwadi residence on Wednesday, bringing an end to the 16-year wait for the civic property to be put to its intended use.
Article Summary: Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation’s new mayoral residence at Adharwadi finally got its first regular occupant. Mayor Harshali Chaudhari-Thavil performed the vastu shanti puja and entered the bungalow on Wednesday.

Article Title: Two held for pledging fake gold chains, taking Rs4.44 lakh from Chakan jeweller
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





Two daily-wage workers were arrested after they allegedly took Rs4.44 lakh from a jeweller in Chakan by allegedly pledging fake gold chains.The duo was identified as Abhijit Gadale (22) of Kesnand and Samir Mane (33) of New Mumbai.Police sub-inspector Pawan Bande of North Chakan police said between July 17 and Sept 9, the duo had pledged three gold chains with the jeweller and taken Rs4.44 lakh against them. “Before giving money to the duo, the jeweller had verified the chains and did not find anything suspicious. The duo had asked the jeweller to melt the chains, if they failed to return the money.”When the jeweller melted the chains, he found they were not made of pure gold. “On Saturday afternoon, the duo again came to the jeweller’s shop and tried to pledge a gold bracelet. The jeweller informed us; we laid a trap and took them into custody. The bracelet they were trying to pledge was made of fake gold as well,” Bande said.“We are investigating whether the duo had similarly cheated other jewellers, and from where they obtained the metal that resembled gold,” Bande added.
Article Summary: The duo was identified as Abhijit Gadale (22) of Kesnand and Samir Mane (33) of New Mumbai. Police said between July 17 and Sept 9, the duo had pledged three gold chains with the jeweller and taken Rs4.44 lakh.

Article Title: Hazari Pahad fire: 4homes wrecked, but no casualties
Article Text:
Nagpur:





A fire that broke out in a slum adjoining Air Force Nagar wall in Hazari Pahad early Monday destroyed household belongings in four houses, two two-wheelers and several LPG cylinders. No casualties were reported as fire brigade personnel swiftly evacuated residents, including women, children and elderly persons, from the affected houses.The fire broke out around 3:30am, reportedly after an incense stick set clothes ablaze at the house of Bhavesh Patil , where clothes had been used to partition the dwelling. The flames soon spread to a two-wheeler belonging to Jyotish Hole. A second two-wheeler was also engulfed, following which the fire spread to Hole’s house. An LPG cylinder blast intensified the blaze, which then spread to adjoining houses.Another two LPG cylinders in the kitchen of Megha Khobragade’s house reportedly exploded, further aggravating the fire. The houses of Patil, Hole, Khobragade and Dhawanlal Bhoyer were gutted, with TVs, refrigerators, clothes and other household articles reduced to ashes.The fire was reported to the civic fire control room by local resident Omprakash Jaiswal. A team from Civil fire station, led by Devanand Shamkule, rushed to the spot, while another team from Trimurti Nagar fire station was also pressed into service. Firefighters first evacuated residents trapped inside the houses and then brought the blaze under control, averting a major mishap.
Article Summary: A fire broke out in a slum adjoining Air Force Nagar wall in Hazari Pahad early Monday. Four houses, two two-wheelers and several LPG cylinders were destroyed. No casualties were reported as fire brigade personnel swiftly evacuated residents.
